'''Ian Hinchliffe''' (born 1952) is a British [[physicist]] at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. 

Hinchliffe studied physics at [[Oxford University]], where he obtained his [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] and in 1977 under the supervision of [[Christopher Llewellyn Smith]] a [[D. Phil]] in theoretical particle physics.<ref name="sakuraiprize"/>

In 1983 he became a Staff Senior Scientist at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, where he served as head of the [[theoretical physics]] group from 1992 to 1999.<ref name="sakuraiprize"/> He is now member emeritus of LBL.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www-theory.lbl.gov/?page_id=10286 |title=LBL Theory: Emeriti |work=lbl.gov |access-date=2025-07-15}}</ref>

Trained in theoretical physics, his primary activity is with the [[ATLAS experiment]] at [[CERN]]'s [[Large Hadron Collider]], which he joined in 1996; he served as ATLAS physics coordinator in 2006–2007 and currently heads Berkeley Lab's ATLAS group. His research emphasizes the importance of experiment in testing theoretical ideas, and in driving theoretical developments aimed at understanding interactions among fundamental particles. Much of his research looks to show how the [[Standard Model]] can be tested at hadron colliders.<ref name="sakuraiprize"/>

In 2011, Ian Hinchliffe, [[Chris Quigg]], [[Estia Eichten]], and [[Kenneth Lane (physicist)|Kenneth Lane]] won the [[Sakurai Prize|J. J. Sakurai Prize for Theoretical Particle Physics]] "for their work, separately and collectively, to chart a course of the exploration of TeV scale physics using multi-TeV hadron colliders".<ref name="sakuraiprize">{{cite web |url=https://newscenter.lbl.gov/2010/10/28/hinchliffe-sakurai/ |title=Berkeley Lab's Ian Hinchliffe Awarded Sakurai Prize in Theoretical Physics |author=Paul Preuss |work=lbl.gov |date=2010-10-28 |access-date=2025-07-15}}</ref>
